messages:
zoe: quick question — you're allowed to run in and rescue one childhood collectible from a burning house. what do you save and why? asking for hypothetical reasons :)

sam: my stuffed whale 'Bubbles'. still smells like my grandma, absolute no-brainer. :sob:

marcus: baseball cards. i have a tiny 1998 Topps set that i'm irrationally proud of. mostly for nostalgia, maybe a small profit later.

priya: the old LEGO space set. i still dream about it. pieces are rare now and i never finished the rocket.

jin: pogs. this is embarrassing but i still have a pog with a foil unicorn. it'd be the weirdest little trophy. :unicorn_face:

luis: Game Boy Pocket + Pokemon Yellow. happiest hours of childhood were with that battery door taped shut. :game_die:

amy: my sticker binder — band stickers, crap from punk shows. feels like a tiny diary.

safety-bot: reminder: actual fire safety first. please do not attempt heroic rescues in real life. fire drill Thursday 3pm. :fire_extinguisher:

zoe: agreed on safety! just curious to see what people hang onto. these are great. :heart:

sam: quick follow-up — anyone actually kept originals boxed? i regret everything about tossing my Tamagotchi box.

priya: i boxed a few LEGO minifigs years ago, sealed in a plastic tote. feels like secret adult hoarding.

marcus: pro tip: put a couple photo shots of the items in cloud storage. then you get nostalgia without the clutter.

luis: true, but no photo replaces that click of the Game Boy buttons.

amy: poll idea: do we keep, digitize, or donate? :raised_hands:

zoe: do a quick react-vote — :thumbsup: keep, :white_check_mark: digitize, :handshake: donate

(small flurry of emoji reactions)

zoe: thanks everyone — great stories. also added a mental note to never throw out band stickers.
